name: Preparing for my Netflix documentary
what: Creator mimes clipping on a lapel mic and sits in an interview chair while on-screen text frames a petty or awkward life event as their Netflix documentary.
origin: Started by TikTok creator @borderbandittx on 16 Jun 2026; posts by @fombasyllah and @wassupa1ex on 30 Jun took it viral.
usage: 438.7K TikTok videos on the sound (20 Oct 2026); top post 35.7M views, 5.7M likes. Anijam says it crossed to Instagram in Oct 2026 (no reel count).
brand_use: Frame a small brand drama as a documentary premise, e.g. 'Preparing for my Netflix documentary about the day we ran out of croissants by 7am.'
risk: Avoid Netflix logos or the Netflix sting; keep the parody generic.
notes: TikTok peaked Jun to Jul 2026; Instagram is the live second wave. Biggest IG post found: jnessa.r, 509K likes, 7 Jul 2026 (https://www.instagram.com/reel/DagSMXqvuGI/), audio not checkable on IG. Old example Dynamite Clothing used an original sound, not On a Mission (55.5K plays, 268 likes), so dropped. The old IG example sherlinanym has 25K likes.

name: Money can't buy happiness, but...
sound: Original audio, eresdigna (Instagram); on TikTok 'suara asli', Nadora | Cycling Journal
what: On-screen text reads 'Money can't buy happiness, but it can buy...' over a short clip of the thing that obviously makes you happy.
origin: The Instagram audio comes from an eresdigna reel posted 25 Nov 2025; the text format took off on it from September 2026.
usage: 316K Instagram reels on the audio and 18.1K TikTok videos on the main TikTok sound (20 Oct 2026); top reel 4.8M views
brand_use: A product shot with a punchline: 'but it can buy' then the hero product or a customer's reaction. Works for retail, food, beauty and experiences.
risk: It reads as an ad, so the reveal has to be genuinely appealing.

examples.note: origin of the audio and top reel on it (eresdigna, 25 Nov 2025)
top TikTok on the sound (curly hair product, 18 Sep 2026)
'best purchase I've ever made' skis (24 Sep 2026)

notes: Instagram reel count is lifetime for the eresdigna audio, so not every reel is this text format. The eresdigna origin reel caption is just '.', so I couldn't confirm from text that it shows the 'but it can buy' line. The TikTok sound is a different clip; captions on it (cosynewbuild, bukii_makeup, stayinginstudio) confirm it carries the trend. Old example @arabellajewelry did not use either sound (it uses a stock jingle) and was dropped. Brand posts on TikTok: Fat Hippo burgers did it on its own original sound (151.7K plays).

name: I just want to be OK
what: Creators dance or act cheerful to the 'I just want to be OK' chorus while the caption reveals the mess or stress they are ignoring.
origin: A 2008 Ingrid Michaelson song, revived on TikTok around 20 to 22 Aug 2026; the earliest big posts found are @madozilla and @camilla.
usage: 204.5K TikTok videos on the sound (20 Oct 2026, includes pre-2026 use); top post 18.5M views, 5M likes
brand_use: Staff dance happily while the caption names a customer headache (tax time, hail claims, a full inbox), then cut to the product sorting it.
risk: Some creators use it for sincere mental-health posts, so keep it light and never mock real distress.

examples.note: 26 Aug 2026, used by SocialBee as the example

notes: The 204.5K count covers all use of the sound since about 2021, so the 2026 share is unknown but clearly large. Biggest posts are late Aug and early Sep, so it is past peak even though round-ups still list it in Oct. Instagram use not verified. Old example @alfiebbrown (1.1M likes) is valid but smaller. Exact first post of the 2026 revival not confirmed.

name: Text message from -A
sound: pll purposes only ty, demi devito
what: On-screen 'text' signed '-A', Pretty Little Liars style, calls out a specific secret habit, over a clip of the creator looking caught out.
origin: The sound dates to Nov 2023; the '-A' text wave started 19 Sep 2026 (@nia.lavine and others), and cast member Shay Mitchell joined on 23 Sep.
usage: 72.1K TikTok videos on the sound (20 Oct 2026), most from 19 to 29 Sep 2026; top post 11.8M views, 2.4M likes
brand_use: '-A' exposes a habit your customers share: 'I saw you add three more to cart at 1am. -A'. Pair it with a reaction shot of a staff member.
risk: Most posts landed in late Sep, so it already feels dated; post now or skip.

examples.note: top post and one of the first of the wave, 19 Sep 2026
PLL cast member Shay Mitchell, 23 Sep 2026

notes: 72.1K includes older non-'-A' uses of the sound since Nov 2023, but the top posts on the page are almost all from the Sep 2026 wave. Later added it on 2 Oct 2026.

name: The Process (process to result)
what: A quick step-by-step of the tools, materials and work behind something, ending on the finished result.
origin: Original audio from Instagram creator @its_drfarah; Later listed the format on 18 Sep 2026. Original reel not found.
usage: 43K Instagram reels on the audio (20 Oct 2026); top reel 138K views
brand_use: Show the making of something: a campaign shoot, a hand-finished product, a dish. Original audio, so it is safe for business accounts.

examples.note: makeup artist process to result, second most-viewed reel (25 Sep 2026)
poster design process for the Broncos (24 Sep 2026)
paid knitting process post, brand use (1 Oct 2026)

notes: Decent volume but no big posts: the top reel (@jieminart, 138K views, a running recap rather than a process video) has hidden likes, and the rest are under 100K views. Mainly a small-business format. No TikTok version found. The original its_drfarah reel isn't among their recent posts.

name: Pray For Me slow-mo entrance
sound: pray for me slo mo, lesgetitrell (slowed edit of Pray For Me, The Weeknd and Kendrick Lamar)
what: Friends run or walk into frame one at a time in exaggerated slow motion, with dramatic faces and poses, timed to the slowed beat.
origin: Dancer @lesgetitrell made the slowed sound and slow-mo routine on 30 Aug 2020; it resurfaced as a group trend in October 2026.
usage: 34.4K TikTok videos on the sound (20 Oct 2026); top post 38M views, top Oct 2026 post 4.2M views
brand_use: Staff take turns making slow-mo hero entrances into the store, kitchen or office. Good for launch days or team culture posts.
risk: Built on a major-label track, so it may be unavailable to business accounts; use a creator partner.
notes: Most-viewed post on the sound is @reboir (38M plays, 7.2M likes, Dec 2022), an older solo use, so the origin is listed first instead. Other Oct 2026 hits: @danya..119 1.5M plays / 226.5K likes, @kennedy_mil18 1.5M / 277.4K. The 34.4K count is lifetime since 2020; the October 2026 wave is a fraction of it but growing fast.

name: Two fishes (Love Island)
what: Lip-sync Sincere's 'two fishes' speech under a caption like 'me explaining to my parents that...', defending a dodgy argument with total conviction.
origin: Peacock posted the Love Island USA Season 8 clip of islander Sincere on 5 Jun 2026; the 'explaining to my parents' lip-sync took off from mid Jun.
usage: 33.9K TikTok videos on the official sound (20 Oct 2026); top post 8.8M views, 1.6M likes
brand_use: Social lead lip-syncs it defending a harmless, slightly unhinged take on the category, e.g. 'me explaining why two desserts is one meal'.
risk: Reality TV audio from a US show many Australians missed; check clearance before using on a brand account.

examples.note: top post doing the 'explaining to my parents' format, 18 Jun 2026

notes: New Engen credits the clip to Corbin Mims (CorbinGPT), but the official Peacock sound is titled SincereFishQuote and top posts tag Sincere, so I went with Sincere. Most top posts are Jun to Jul 2026; the Oct bump is mostly Halloween costumes (e.g. @hashtagrealaf, 523K likes, 10 Oct). Re-uploaded copies of the audio exist, so 33.9K undercounts total use.

name: Ceiling fan outfit transition
sound: Girls on Film, Duran Duran (Instagram; TikTok sounds vary)
what: Filmed from above while lying under a ceiling fan; each blade pass wipes to a new outfit, usually four looks in about 15 seconds, often AI-generated.
origin: Went viral on TikTok in the week of 28 Sep 2026 (The Tab); a CapCut fan-transition template was circulating from late Aug. Original creator not confirmed.
usage: 33K Instagram Reels on 'Girls on Film' (SocialPilot, 12 to 25 Oct 2026); top TikTok post 3.3M views, 259K likes
brand_use: A fashion or homewares brand runs four products in one fan spin, ending on the price or shop link.
risk: 'Girls on Film' is restricted for business accounts, so use a cleared sound. Many viral versions are AI; label it if the client's is.

examples.note: most-liked post found, real (non-AI) version, 6 Oct 2026

notes: No single TikTok sound: the top posts use generic original sounds (locket4mads, prettylittlepryncess), so audio_verified is false; the trend is the visual format. No TikTok Girls on Film fan posts found in the sound's top list. usage_n is the Instagram audio count only, so true usage is higher. TikTok hashtag counts were blocked by a captcha. Old examples were small (@sessilygoo 6.1K likes, @nickytalksalot 17.6K likes, a tutorial).

name: "Let's…" Sean O'Pry snap edit
what: Creator lies deadpan or asleep through dull prompts ('Let's play Fortnite'), then their favourite thing is named and it cuts to the Sean O'Pry finger-snap edit.
origin: @.fwmatu's Sean O'Pry edit (a 2015 Paco Rabanne ad) on 9 Sep 2026 started it; the 'Let's…' skit version took off on TikTok in late Sep 2026.
usage: 24.9K TikTok videos on the main sound plus 5,777 on @.fwmatu's original (20 Oct 2026); top skit 22.9M views, 4.3M likes.
brand_use: 'Let's meal prep' gets nothing, 'Let's go to the gym' gets nothing, 'Let's get [brand] gelato' gets the full snap edit.
risk: The edit uses footage of a real model from a Paco Rabanne ad; brands should restage the hype half rather than use that clip.

examples.note: top 'Let's' skit post, 10 Oct 2026 (ZHC, 'I failed history')
'Lets play Fortnite' vs Roblox horror games, 26 Sep 2026
origin of the edit, 9 Sep 2026; same song uploaded as 'original sound - matu'

notes: SocialBee's 'Let's…' (14 Oct) is this trend; its IG example ayo.ogunajala 'Let's go to Lidl' has 397K likes, 1 Oct 2026 (https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dd-OHxPoFWQ/), tagged #seanopry. Format confirmed from screenshots of the two skit examples. The song is split across several uploads, so usage_n (sum of two sound pages) undercounts. Origin is the plain edit, not the skit format.

name: Look, a spider (couples)
what: One person says 'look, a spider' and their partner or friend leaps into their arms in panic; variations swap in a scarier or more personal fear.
origin: Spanish-language TikTok user @user077983456 posted the original friends clip on 19 Mar 2025; it was revived by couples in Aug and Sep 2026.
usage: 6,661 TikTok videos on the sound (20 Oct 2026); top post 21.6M views, 1.9M likes
brand_use: Swap the spider for a customer fear: 'look, a parking fine' gets the leap, 'look, the app paid it' gets a calm shrug. Suits apps and services.
notes: Low video count (6.7K) but several posts over 1M likes, so it is a views-heavy, low-participation trend. Old example @lottekln (17.4K likes) uses the sound but is small, so it was dropped. Ramdam's app version (panic at a manual task, calm with the app) is a niche spin, not the main format.

name: GRWM loading 0% to 100%
sound: original sound, saff (@saffknight) on TikTok; Windows in Brazil (Sped Up) on Instagram
what: A get-ready-with-me that starts at '0%' in robe and eye patches, with a loading percentage climbing each cut until the finished look at 100%.
origin: TikTok creator @saffknight posted the first version with her original sound on 2 Oct 2026; Later listed the Instagram version the same day.
usage: 5,687 TikTok videos on the sound (20 Oct 2026), up from zero on 2 Oct; top post 8.2M views, 684K likes.
brand_use: Load a product build from 0% to 100%: a cafe plating its signature dish, or a detailer taking a muddy ute to showroom finish.
notes: Two audios: TikTok runs on saff's original sound; Later and Anijam name 'Windows in Brazil (Sped Up)' for Reels (https://www.instagram.com/reels/audio/1094115923496866/), but I could not load the IG audio page for a reel count. IG example raychen.lei, 65K likes, 2 Oct 2026 (https://www.instagram.com/reel/DeAmc__TMqX/). Old TikTok examples danaarose (4.5K likes) and imabbysigua (1.4K likes) do use the right sound but are small. Fast growth: 5.7K videos in 18 days.

name: we fell in love in october
sound: we fell in love in october, girl in red
what: Soft autumn montages set to the song: cosy outfits, baking, pumpkins, coffee, pets and slow afternoons.
origin: girl in red released the song in 2018; it returns as the go-to October sound every year.
usage: 2.1M TikTok videos and 1M Instagram reels on the sound (20 Oct 2026); top Oct 2026 post 45.4M views
brand_use: A cafe or homewares brand can cut a mood piece of its seasonal range. In Australia, flip it to spring: jacarandas, iced coffee, first swims.
risk: The autumn look is northern hemisphere, so localise it for spring.

examples.note: top post on the sound (7 Oct 2026)
pumpkin sourdough bake, food angle (17 Jul 2026)

notes: Counts are lifetime for the sound (it gets reused every year), not just 2026. New Engen (14 Oct 2026) cites it as #1 on MusicMaestro's US TikTok trending sounds chart for week 40. Major-label track, may be restricted for business accounts.

name: Pumpkin Head trend
sound: Oh Klahoma, Jack Stauber (most common; many use other sounds)
what: Friends, couples or families wear hollowed carved pumpkins over their heads and stage an everyday scene or photoshoot, set to 'Oh Klahoma'.
origin: Began as the pumpkin head photoshoot in autumn 2020 (Know Your Meme); returns every October, with a 2026 wave led by @the_life_of_aivax on 25 Sep.
usage: 548.6K TikTok videos on 'Oh Klahoma' (20 Oct 2026, all years since 2020); top 2026 post 8.1M views, 1.8M likes
brand_use: Staff wear pumpkin heads while doing their normal jobs (barista, mechanic, receptionist) for a one-off Halloween post.
risk: Halloween-only and a weaker moment in Australia, where it is spring.

examples.note: top 2026 post, family kitchen scene, 25 Sep 2026
besties photoshoot, own original sound, 17 Oct 2026
couple photoshoot on Oh Klahoma, 2 Sep 2026

notes: Renamed from 'Pumpkin Head Illusion'. The forced-perspective illusion New Engen describes is weak: the only post found (@eb_ness_x, via vadbav.com) has 60 likes, and no named sound or count exists. The old examples were poor (@htx.abby115 had 39 likes). The real 2026 trend is the wearable pumpkin head version. The 548.6K sound count is all-time, so the 2026 figure is much lower and unknown. Sound varies a lot; only 'Oh Klahoma' recurs.

name: Goo Goo Muck Halloween reels
what: Spooky clips cut to the beat: bedsheet ghost photoshoots, Halloween decor and props, and costume shots.
origin: The Cramps song (1981) went viral with the Wednesday Addams dance from Netflix's Wednesday in late 2022 and now returns every Halloween.
usage: 316K Instagram reels and 204.2K TikTok videos on the sound (20 Oct 2026, lifetime); top Oct 2026 reel 347K views
brand_use: Put the team under bedsheets for a ghost photoshoot in the store or office, cut to the beat. Easy for salons, bars and retail.
risk: Major-label track, restricted for business accounts, so use a creator partner.

examples.note: top recent reel on the audio, ghost photoshoot (27 Sep 2026)
hair salon brand use, 'spooky habits' (1 Oct 2026)

notes: SocialPilot frames it as 'POV: your Halloween decoration is alive', but the top 2026 reels on the audio are ghost photoshoots and Halloween montages; I found no big 'decoration comes alive' post, so I renamed it. Counts are lifetime and include the 2022 Wednesday dance wave. This year's posts are modest (best ~21K likes). TikTok 2026 posts on the official sound were small (e.g. @buttercranecentre office ghost shoot, 1.6K plays); bigger TikToks use lyric edits on other 'original sound' uploads, so they were excluded. Plays for Instagram are the view counts shown on the audio page.

name: Ramalama costume walk
what: Camera low on the creator's legs as they strut slowly towards the lens, then on the beat it cuts to reveal the full Halloween costume.
origin: Walk versions appeared in late Jul 2025; @swaggy_cucumber's Hocus Pocus group walk on 1 Oct 2025 made it the Halloween costume-reveal format. Revived Oct 2026.
usage: 473.9K TikTok videos on the sound (20 Oct 2026, up from about 430.7K quoted by RouteNote earlier in Oct); top post 94.3M views
brand_use: Swap the costume for a product or a staff uniform: slow walk-up on the shoes, cut to the full reveal of a new range or fit-out.
risk: Halloween is smaller in Australia and the window closes 31 Oct; check the track is cleared for brand accounts.

examples.note: top post, 1 Oct 2025, the post that set the Halloween version

notes: Video count read off the rendered TikTok sound page on 20 Oct 2026. No source names a single originator of the walk; RouteNote says early walk versions date to late Jul 2025. Swaggy_cucumber's post is the earliest of the top posts on the sound page.

name: October is all about me
sound: alkuperäinen ääni (Drake 'Slime You Out' line), J
what: Creators lip-sync the Drake 'October is all about me' line to camera, often with birthday-month or Libra-season text on screen.
origin: The sound clip was posted by TikTok user J (@user2267783) on 21 Sep 2026 in a Libra birthday-month video.
usage: 14.3K TikTok videos on the sound (20 Oct 2026); top post 929K views, 160K likes
brand_use: A brand with an October launch or birthday posts a staff member lip-syncing the line over the new product. It only works until 31 Oct.
risk: Dead on 1 Nov. Uses a Drake recording, so check commercial clearance before a business account posts it.
notes: Small but real: 14.3K videos, biggest post 160K likes. Old example @ciaralillyyy (66.5K likes) does use the sound but is smaller, so it was dropped. Other re-uploads of the Drake line may exist on other sound ids; not counted.
